1.
Supplementary affidavit filed today on behalf of the applicant is taken on record.
2. None appeared on behalf of the informant even in the revised call.

3. Heard Sri Indra Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the applicant and Dr.S.B.Maurya, learned AGA-I, for the State.
4.

The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
473 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 304B, 452, 323, 504, 506 IPC and under section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Kotwali Nagar, District Etah, during pendency of the trial.

marriage of the applicant was performed with the deceased on 25.11.2020 and after marriage,
applicant and his family members tortured her for additional demand of Rs. Five lacs and due to Amit Jauhari vs State Of U.P. on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180261795/

sentences.text: 6. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is the husband of the deceased and on the basis of false allegation he has been made accused in the present matter and he neither ever tortured the deceased nor ever demanded any dowry.

7. He further submits that actually deceased herself left her matrimonial home and started living in her paternal home but after her death a false story has been cooked up by her father and applicant and his family members were made accused in the present matter.

8. He further submits that admittedly deceased died on 6.6.2023 and FIR of the present case was lodged through an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. and even application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. was moved after more than a week and thereafter FIR of the present case was lodged and this fact clearly suggests that FIR is based on false and frivolous facts.
9.
He further submits that post mortem report of the deceased suggests that she died due to cardiac arrest as a result of septicemic shock.

10. He next argued that according to the post mortem report, deceased was having pus in her lungs and in her both the intestines and lungs have also been shrinked and this fact shows that while she was residing in her paternal home, she developed some serious complications and due to medical condition, she expired.
11. He further submits that however applicant was also made accused in another case but in that case after investigation final report has been submitted.
12. He further submits that applicant is not having any previous criminal history and in the present matter he is in jail since 28.7.2023.

13. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayerfor bail and submits that applicant is the husband of the deceased and there is specific allegation in the FIR that applicant and his family members tortured the deceased for dowry and they turned her out from her matrimonial home and when she started living with her parents then they arrived at her paternal home and made assault and due to assault made by them she died but he could not dispute the fact that post mortem report of the deceased suggests that deceased died due to cardiac arrest as a result of septicemic shock.
14.

Learned AGA further could not dispute the fact that according to the post mortem report of the deceased, her both the lungs and intestines were filled with pus and after three months of alleged assault she died.
He further could not dispute, there is no medical report of deceased on record with regard to assault.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 15. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

16. However, applicant is the husband of the deceased and his wife died within seven years of her marriage and there is also allegation of demand of dowry but admitted facts of the case is that at the time of incident deceased was residing in her paternal home.

However, according to the FIR, while deceased was residing in her paternal home, applicant and his family members arrived there on 8.3.2023 and made assault and due to assault made by them she sustained injuries and thereafter due to injury she succumbed on 6.6.2023, i.e., after about three months but there is no medical report of the deceased on record with regard to the alleged incident of assault dated 8.3.2023 and,
therefore, at this stage it cannot be said that deceased died on 6.6.2023 due to the assault made by accused persons on 8.3.2023.

17. Further, post mortem report of the deceased suggests that cause of death was due to cardiac arrest as a result of septicemic shock due to ante mortem injury and from the perusal of the ante mortem injury, it reflects that deceased was not having any external injury but her lungs and intestines were having pus and her lungs have also been shrinked, therefore, arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant that deceased while living at her paternal home developed some serious lungs and intestinal disease and due to her medical condition she expired on 6.6.2023 during treatment cannot be completely brushed aside.

18.Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
19. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

20. Let the applicant-Amit Jauhari be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
21. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

22.
